steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: On 29 October 1929, the American stock market crashed (Wall Street Crash). American banks recalled loans from Germany, causing economic collapse. By 1932, 6 million Germans were unemployed (over 30% of the workforce), and industrial production fell by 58% from its 1929 level.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: In the 1928 election, the Nazis won just 2.6% of the vote (12 seats). By July 1932, they were the largest party with 37.3% of the vote (230 seats). This extraordinary rise was driven by the economic crisis and the failure of mainstream parties to solve it.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nazis were NOT primarily a working-class party. Their strongest support came from the Protestant middle class, farmers, and small-town voters. The working class largely continued to support the SPD or KPD. However, the Nazis did make some inroads into the working class through the SA, which offered unemployed men food, comradeship and a sense of purpose.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Joseph Goebbels was appointed Nazi Party propaganda leader in 1929. He controlled the Nazi message with extraordinary skill, using every available medium to reach the German people. He said: "The essence of propaganda consists in winning people over to an idea so sincerely, so vitally, that in the end they succumb to it and can never escape."

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why the Wall Street Crash helped the Nazis. (4 marks) | How important was propaganda in the rise of the Nazis? (8 marks) | "The Nazis rose to power because of the economic crisis." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the election statistics: 2.6% (1928) → 18.3% (1930) → 37.3% (July 1932) → 33.1% (November 1932) Always distinguish between WHY the Nazis became popular and WHY Hitler became Chancellor - they are different questions The Nazis never won a majority in a free election - Hitler became Chancellor through a political deal, not a democratic mandate For "why did people support the Nazis" questions, use specific groups (middle class, farmers, unemployed, business leaders) Remember von Papen's quote: "We've hired him" - it shows how catastrophically the elites underestimated Hitler The Wall Street Crash (29 October 1929) was the turning point - Stresemann died on 3 October 1929, just weeks before Link the SA to both support (comradeship for the unemployed) and intimidation (violence against opp
